correctness.rationale: The first eigenspace is the complexification of traceless quaternionic-Hermitian quadratic forms, whose real dimension is 2d^2-d-1. Stabilizer invariance splits it orthogonally into axial, cross and tangential blocks. Their exact cap Gram ratios are beta-weighted moments with shapes (2,2d-2), (3,2d-1) and (2,2d). Exact algebra yields positive eigenvalues and three pairwise factorizations, uniquely establishing the two sharp extrema transitions and multiplicities. The fixed-volume limit follows by monotone inversion of cap volume. The included checker computes radial integrals with exact rational antiderivatives and tests the trace identity in 60 cases, not as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: Complete first-harmonic spectral stability across every quaternionic projective dimension \(d\ge3\) is a natural missing precision beyond known large-sieve bounds. Its two independent optimizer changes, exact condition-number law, and two universal cap-volume transitions are structural, not arbitrary single-dimension numerics; they distinguish quaternionic from complex projective recovery geometries. Larger harmonic cutoffs and discrete sampling are explicitly not claimed.
